newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi and Yemen end new round of border talks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi and Yemen end new round of border talks.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and Yemen on Wednesday ended a new round of talks in Sanaa aimed at settling a long-standing border dispute, Gulf regional news agencies said.
Officials from both sides discussed border demarcation between the oil giant kingdom and its impoverished Arab neighbour. They would hold another meeting in Saudi Arabia in June, the agencies added.
Yemen has hinted it might resort to international arbitration if more than a year of talks with Riyadh fail to settle the 60-year-old border row.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen had several minor clashes in a border area potentially rich in oil and gas before the two sides signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the dispute.
Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh had in the summer complained that the committee was making slow progress and called for a summit with Saudi Arabia to speed up the talks.
The committee has met scores of times since 1995.

Yemen's relations with Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, have improved in the last few years. Sanaa angered its Gulf Arab neighbours when it appeared to side with Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis over Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
